tasks.title: Cross-request payment replay and requirement substitution are rejected
tasks.description: Threat model: settled payment evidence quoted against one PaymentRequirements set (price, recipient, asset, network, resource) must never authorise a different, more expensive or otherwise unauthorised request. The exact scheme binds amount, asset and payTo on chain, and the memo binds nonce uniqueness, but no scheme field cryptographically binds the protected resource; the verifier therefore enforces the binding at the trust boundary by recording the requirements hash a transaction was verified under and refusing the same transaction against any different requirements set. Acceptance criteria AC01-AC08 below are the required security outcomes; the formal core each sandbox check runs is deliberately small and does not bound the natural-language claim.

tasks.title: R20: a client retry never pays twice for one request

tasks.title: R24: null, empty and non-object payment headers, and the V1 X-PAYMENT header
tasks.description: R24 today sends five PAYMENT-SIGNATURE values (not base64, base64 that is not JSON, and a JSON array, string and number). This extends the same check to the shapes it does not yet cover: the JSON literal null, the booleans true and false, an empty JSON object {}, a JSON object whose required members are null ({"x402Version":2,"accepted":null,"payload":null}), an empty header value, and a header value of only whitespace. It also sends every value in the V1 X-PAYMENT header when the route advertises x402Version 1, because V1 servers decode that header with separate code. The absent header is graded as the control: it must get 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED (V2) or a V1 JSON body with accepts. Each malformed value passes only if the answer is 402 or 400 with a structured error (a PAYMENT-REQUIRED that decodes to a PaymentRequired object, or a JSON body with an error field), the facilitator double records no /verify and no /settle for it, the protected content is not returned, the connection is not dropped, and the server still answers the absent-header control with 402 after the batch (it is still up). A 5xx, a dropped connection, a 2xx, a facilitator call or a dead server after the batch fails the check. Requests are paced at least 5 s apart against live servers, as in R24.

tasks.description: I run the suite for a project for free. Terms: one free initial run, then queued reruns on new releases only (never on every commit) for six months from consent, recorded as program_start and program_end in matrix/rows/<slug>.json. In return the project is listed with its results, displays the badge in its README with attribution to Optitransfer/x402-conformance (the copy-paste snippet is the badge plus 'Conformance tested by [Optitransfer/x402-conformance](row link)'), and installs the notify hook. Consent: the form's required checkbox 'Display the badge in our README with attribution to Optitransfer/x402-conformance', and the free-run checkbox for the hook, with the public testnet endpoint. (1) docs/templates/x402-conformance-notify.yml, for the project's repository as .github/workflows/x402-conformance-notify.yml, runs on release published only and comments `/x402-conformance run slug= repo= ref=<tag> version=` on the row's own issue; repository_dispatch with the same fields is also accepted. (2) .github/workflows/run-queue.yml and tools/run_queue.py: enqueue accepts a request only for a listed row in the program, inside its program window, on the row's own issue by its contact or the issue's author, for the row's own repository, with a release tag (a bare commit is refused); one entry per slug in matrix/queue/<slug>.json on the run-queue branch, so duplicates collapse and a ref already run is not run again; the first run is queued automatically once the row is listed. The runner works within matrix/queue/caps.json (runs per day, hours between runs of one slug, probes at least 5 s apart, testnet and devnet ids only) and refuses to run if the caps allow any spend. The queue never runs the project's code: it checks out this suite at the pinned release tag and sends unpaid, paced GETs to the project's public testnet endpoint (tier 1, XC-98), so nothing is paid, signed on chain or sent to a hosted facilitator or mainnet. That job has read-only permissions and no secrets. (3) Full results go to the project privately first: the run's evidence is sealed (age) to the maintainer's key, the project is told on its issue that the results will reach it privately, and only a maintainer's `/x402-conformance publish slug= run=` comment unseals it, passes it through tools/row_from_evidence.py and opens the row's pull request for review; a failing check follows SECURITY.md. Nothing merges automatically. (4) The weekly freshness job stays as the backstop, reads each project's public README through the API (a plain read, no referrer, nothing embedded) and flags a row whose README no longer links its row or badge, and opens a renewal heads-up issue at five months. After program_end the row stays listed with its last result, marked stale, and the badge greys out; nothing is deleted. Self-runs with the Action stay free and unlimited. docs/MATRIX.md and docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md have a 'Free run program' section with these terms.

tasks.description: Every listed row has a tier. Tier 1, External-verified: the checks that work from outside the project's stack (P1-P7, P9 and P10: unpaid, paced GETs of the paid URL and its /.well-known/x402). The run queue (XC-97) runs them on each new release (notify hook or weekly release check) against the row's public testnet endpoint, with this suite checked out at the release pinned in matrix/queue/suite.json; it never checks out or runs the project's code and spends nothing. Badge: 'External-verified · x402-conformance <tag> · Optitransfer', with checks passed out of applicable and the date. Tier 2, Full suite (self-hosted): the whole suite runs only in the project's own CI, on each release, through the Action with `attest: true`. src/x402conf/tiers.py writes x402-conformance-attestation.json: format x402-conformance.attestation/1, the suite repository, ref and version, the project's repository, tag, commit, workflow and run, a timestamp, and one entry per catalogue check (pass, fail, warn, not_applicable with a reason from the `not-applicable` input, or not_run). actions/attest-build-provenance signs it with the job's GitHub OIDC identity (Sigstore) and the Action uploads it as x402-conformance-attestation-<row>. It is submitted by the notify hook's `/x402-conformance attest slug= repo= ref= run=` comment or repository_dispatch, by the form's optional run link, or found by the weekly job. The queue verifies and does not run: it downloads only that file, runs `gh attestation verify` with the row's repository, the attested commit and tag and the GitHub OIDC issuer, and tools/attestation.py checks that the signed digest is this file, the identity matches the row's repository, commit, tag and run, every check pinned in suite.json is present, and each not-applicable check has a reason. An attestation from another suite release is listed with 'rerun on current suite' and a grey badge. Verified, the attestation is committed as matrix/attestations/<slug>.json and the row becomes tier 2 with the badge 'Full suite (self-hosted) · x402-conformance <tag> · Optitransfer'. The signature proves where and on which commit the run happened, not that the results were not altered; docs/MATRIX.md says so. Rows show the tier, checks passed / applicable, the failed count, the denominator (exercised / NA / needs self-hosted), the suite tag and the date. The six-month free window (XC-97) covers tier-1 reruns and tier-2 verification and listing; a full run on hosted staging is the exception, by arrangement with written permission. Badge, snippet and attribution to Optitransfer/x402-conformance are unchanged. docs/MATRIX.md, docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md, docs/BADGE.md, the row schema, the issue form and the example row (one tier-1 example) are updated. tasks.description: Tier 1 (XC-98) grows from 9 to 11 checks. src/x402conf/external.py ports ts/src/head-unpaid.ts and ts/src/header.ts to Python, graded the same way, and `x402conf resource` gains --malformed-header (R24: one unpaid GET per malformed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE value, the same five values as MALFORMED_HEADERS in ts/src/header.ts, in the same order) and --unpaid-head (R16a: one unpaid HEAD; it passes on 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED offer or on 405 without PAYMENT-RESPONSE). Both reuse the GET that P1-P7 already sent and go through the run's pacer: at least 5 s apart off loopback, and a request over --max-requests is not sent and the check is reported skipped. A HEAD is not a GET, so off loopback it is sent only with --operator-permission <ref>, the devnet runner's convention for the operator's written permission, which the results record; without it R16a is skipped and the rest still runs. `x402conf-svm live` follows the same rule (on loopback it still grades P1-P7, R16a and R24 in 7 requests, XC-88). The 'Add or update my row' form gains an optional box, 'also allow one unpaid HEAD request per tier-1 run', stored as consent.unpaid_head; that box is the operator's permission, and the queue's `run` job passes the row's consent issue as --operator-permission only when it is ticked. The run job sends at most eight requests (P1-P7 and P9 on one GET, P10 on one GET of /.well-known/x402, R24 on five GETs, R16a on one HEAD), all unpaid, no facilitator call, no mainnet, zero spend, and never checks out the project's code. An external check the run did not reach (R16a without permission) counts as needing the self-hosted run. The example row becomes 8/9, '9 exercised / 2 NA / 68 needs self-hosted'. XC-90's extra R24 values, once signed, land in both lists together; criterion AC03 keeps them equal.

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.

Testnet only: never use a mainnet CAIP-2 id as a payment target, never fund a key with anything but testnet faucet tokens, never call a hosted facilitator; every facilitator under test is the loopback double or my own instance on 127.0.0.1.

Zero spend and unpaid only: if a check would need a payment, a signature, a facilitator call or a request other than GET or the one permitted HEAD off loopback, STOP and report. Never send the HEAD off loopback without --operator-permission, and never more than eight requests a run.

Opt-in only: nothing about a project is committed (no row, no name in a table, no evidence, no badge) until it accepts through the 'Add or update my row' form or a pull request, with the consent recorded there. The outreach list is private and never committed. If a criterion seems to need a row for a project that has not accepted, STOP and report.
